title: Customer Failover Simulation Ladder and QA Harness
author: Evan Cheng
body:
Overview

This playbook describes a progressive failover simulation ladder and a lightweight QA harness intended for use during enterprise onboarding, Dedicated cutovers, or scheduled resilience drills. The ladder gives customer success, SRE, and engineering teams a safe, repeatable set of scenarios that increase in impact, from low-risk smoke tests to full-region failovers. The QA harness provides automation snippets, acceptance criteria, and a post-test report template to accelerate validation and QBR artifacts.

Scope

- Applies to Hosted, Dedicated, and Private customers running production traffic via the Redwood API or Dedicated pools.
- Focus areas: model serving availability, routing/fallback, KV/prefix cache behavior, telemetry continuity, and cost/safety controls.
- Not within scope: changes to customer production data stores outside Redwood endpoints, third-party cloud provider restoration steps (except as monitored outcomes).

Definitions

- Simulation Ladder: ordered list of test scenarios from non-disruptive to high-impact.
- QA Harness: scripts, monitors, and reporting templates used to execute and validate simulations.
- Safety Net: automatic rollback and throttles that stop escalation to higher-impact tests.

Roles & Responsibilities

- Customer Success (CS): coordinate stakeholders, own run cadence and communication, validate customer-facing acceptance.
- SRE/Infra: execute or supervise infrastructure-level simulations (region failover, routing swaps), own monitoring dashboards and rollback hooks.
- Serving Runtime/Platform Eng: own model fallback behavior, ensure KV cache metrics and model variants are instrumented.
- Customer Technical Lead: give final go/no-go and confirm customer-side prerequisites.

Prerequisites (Checklist)

1) Formal sign-off from customer technical lead and CS (email thread or Confluence approval).
2) Snapshot of important configs: active model version pins, rollout policies, per-customer routing policy, rate-limit allowances.
3) Enable test telemetry namespace: prefix telemetry streams with "test/<customer-id>/failover-<date>" to avoid mixed QBR data.
4) Ensure a canary production token with restricted quotas (quota <= 5% of normal traffic).
5) Runbook distribution: all participants have access to the incident channel, dashboard links, and the rollback CLI.
6) Backup of KV cache snapshot (where feasible) and export of recent evals and prompt sets.

Simulation Ladder (ordered scenarios)

1. Canary Request Integrity (Minimal risk)
   - Objective: confirm routing, authentication, and response structure.
   - Actions: send 100 synthetic requests via customer canary token with both streaming and non-streaming paths.
   - Acceptance: 95% success rate, p95 latency within 1.5x baseline.

2. Model Variant Fallback (Low risk)
   - Objective: validate automatic fallback from primary model to smaller/quantized variant.
   - Actions: temporarily change routing policy for canary requests to mark primary as "unavailable" via feature flag.
   - Acceptance: Responses continue with expected error-free output; quality degradation check using 20 short eval prompts (min BLEU/ROUGE thresholds defined per customer).

3. KV Prefix Cache Eviction (Medium risk)
   - Objective: test behavior when prefix/KV cache is evicted/invalidated.
   - Actions: trigger cache eviction for canary keys using admin API: POST /admin/cache/evict {"customer":"<id>", "prefix":"/chat/"}.
   - Acceptance: cold-start latency aligns with documented cold-cache baseline (p95 within 2x), no request loss, metrics show cache-miss spike and recovery.

4. Gradual Capacity Throttle (Medium-high risk)
   - Objective: confirm throttles and quota-protector behavior under sustained pressure.
   - Actions: ramp canary qps from 1 -> 100 over 10 minutes using load tool.
   - Acceptance: per-customer rate-limit webhook fires, no global degradation, SLOs maintained for other tenants.

5. Region Routing Swap (High risk; SRE execute)
   - Objective: validate cross-region routing, data residency compliance and cold-cache impact.
   - Actions: update routing policy to move canary traffic from primary region to secondary region.
   - Acceptance: customer traffic remains available (>=90% success during event), trace continuity preserved, and telemetry shows expected latency jump but no errors beyond defined burst thresholds (5xx <= 2%).

6. Simulated Model Heap/Kernel OOM (High risk; platform eng)
   - Objective: exercise model-level degradation and automatic fallback to compatible variants.
   - Actions: toggle runtime feature to simulate kernel OOM for a model instance, observe rollback/fallback.
   - Acceptance: fallback invoked within configured timeout, user requests get served by alternative variant with bounded latency and no silent failures.

7. Controlled Full Failover (Critical; scheduled)
   - Objective: end-to-end failover to alternate control plane path or secondary cluster.
   - Actions: SRE take primary cluster out of service for canary and non-critical traffic (with customer approval for non-critical) and shift traffic.
   - Acceptance: Redwood maintains available endpoints with configured fallback, customer verifies core flows in <2 hours and signs off.

Execution Playbook (per Scenario)

- Pre-start (15–60 minutes): Confirm participants, clear window, snapshot dashboards (links below), and set channel to "simulation" mode in status tool.
- Start: Execute the harness runner for the scenario (examples below). Capture logs to centralized test bucket and mark telemetry namespace.
- Observe: dedicated observer tracks primary metrics (see Monitoring & Acceptance Criteria).
- Pause & Decision: After each test step, a 10-minute decision window for customer technical lead to proceed or abort.
- Rollback: use automated rollback CLI (example). If rollback fails, escalate immediately to SRE + Platform Eng.

Monitoring & Acceptance Criteria

Primary signals (monitored in the Redwood Console):
- Availability: success_rate(checks) >= defined acceptance rate (see each scenario).
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 compared to baseline; baseline should be collected 24–72 hours pre-sim.
- Errors: 5xx_rate <= 2% during high-impact tests; localized error spikes must not exceed 5% for longer than 10 minutes.
- Quota/Throttles: number of rate-limit webhook events; alerts at >10 events/min.
- Telemetry continuity: traces per request (distributed tracing) should retain root span and attach fallback indicators.

Acceptance Table (example thresholds)

| Signal | Low-impact | Medium | High-impact | Critical |
|--------|-----------:|-------:|-----------:|--------:|
| Success rate | >= 98% | >= 95% | >= 90% | >= 85% |
| p95 latency | <= 1.5x baseline | <= 2x baseline | <= 3x baseline | <= 4x baseline |
| 5xx rate | <= 0.5% | <= 1% | <= 2% | <= 3% |

Communication Templates

- Pre-test announcement (email / incident channel):
  Subject: [Sim] <Customer> Failover Simulation – <date/time>
  Body: short summary, expected impact (canary only vs non-critical), duration, rollback plan, participant list, and observability links.

- Abort notice:
  Subject: [Sim ABORTED] <Customer> Failover Simulation – <date/time>
  Body: reason, immediate next steps, and owner for post-mortem.

- Completion/Signoff:
  Subject: [Sim COMPLETE] <Customer> Failover Simulation – <date/time>
  Body: pass/fail, metrics snapshot, follow-ups, and QBR artifact location.

Automation & CLI Snippets (QA Harness)

- Run synthetic canary (curl example):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer <CANARY_TOKEN>" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '{"model":"rwd-32k-1","input":"Canary ping","metadata":{"test":"failover-2026-01-28"}}'

- Evict KV cache (admin API):
  curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.ai/v1/cache/evict \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer <ADMIN_KEY>" \n    -d '{"customer":"<id>","prefix":"/chat/"}'

- Sample harness runner (Python pseudo):
  #!/usr/bin/env python3
  import requests, time
  for i in range(100):
      r = requests.post("https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate", headers={"Authorization":"Bearer <CANARY_TOKEN>"}, json={"model":"rwd-8k-fallback","input":"sim"})
      print(r.status_code)
      time.sleep(0.5)

Rollback CLI (single command):
  redwood infra routing restore --customer <id> --timestamp $(date -u +%s)

Post-simulation Report (template)

- Title: <Customer> Failover Simulation – <date/time>
- Summary: one paragraph with outcome and whether test progressed ladder.
- Timeline: chronological bullets with minutes and actions.
- Key Metrics: success_rate, p95 latency, 5xx count, cache-miss rate.
- Findings: list of issues discovered, prioritized.
- Action Items: owner, ETA, severity.
- QBR Artifacts: links to dashboards, exported graphs, and telemetry raw exports.

Integration with QBRs and Health Checks

- Tag simulation runs with the customer QBR project in telemetry to ensure runs are excluded from long-term baseline calculations unless explicitly included.
- Add major findings and remediations as agenda items in the next QBR; use the Post-simulation Report as a one-page appendix.

Safety & Compliance Notes

- For regulated customers, ensure data residency controls are preserved: if routing to another region violates residency, do not run region swap tests until legal sign-off.
- DO NOT run controlled full failover for customers with active compliance hold or pending audit without Security/Legal approval.

Appendix: Helpful Dashboard Links (examples)

- Redwood Console – Customer <id> Overview: https://console.redwood.ai/customers/<id>
- Sim telemetry namespace (example): telemetry://test/<id>/failover-2026-01-28
- Rate-limit webhook history: https://console.redwood.ai/telemetry/ratelimit/<id>

Appendix: Quick Troubleshooting Steps

- If synthetic requests return 401: check canary token expiry and token-scoping controls.
- If p95 latency balloons >4x baseline: pause test, capture runtime heap and GPU metrics, and open SRE channel.
- If KV cache eviction causes silent failures: restore snapshot and escalate to platform eng; mark quota to fail-open if required.

Revision History

Related Artifacts

- Stored run results and raw telemetry should be exported to: s3://redwood-simulations/<customer-id>/<date>/ and linked in the Post-simulation Report.
